question: A patellar fracture with a palpable gap > 3 mm and inability to perform a straight-leg raise is an indication for operative fixation with tension-band wiring.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The two criteria for operative patellar fixation are: displacement > 3 mm AND disrupted extensor mechanism (inability to perform straight-leg raise). Tension-band wiring is the standard technique.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Operative fixation is indicated when displacement exceeds 3 mm AND the extensor mechanism is disrupted (demonstrated by failure of straight-leg raise). Tension-band wiring converts the distraction force of the quadriceps into compression across the fracture.
